Most smart home lighting options rely on small bulbs and plug-in adapters, but as the market matures, we're starting to see full recessed ceiling fixtures with native Apple Home support (via Matter). SwitchBot has just launched its new SwitchBot RGBICWW Ceiling Light, which delivers high-brightness illumination and ships with native Matter support right out of the box.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to the Apple smart home framework.

Native Matter and Apple Home Integration

The most important feature of this new ceiling light is that it operates entirely without a SwitchBot Hub and supports Matter out of the box. As long as your Apple TV 4K or HomePod stays connected, the fixture can join your existing ecosystem directly over a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network.

Size and Brightness Specifications

SwitchBot offers two sizes to suit different scenarios: the 12-inch model targets hallways and bathrooms with 2,000 lumens of brightness; the larger 15-inch model is suited to living rooms and bedrooms, pushing up to 3,200 lumens. It also features stepless dimming, allowing brightness to be smoothly adjusted from 100% all the way down to 0%.

Most standard smart bulbs usually only let you pick one color at a time, but this fixture uses RGBIC technology, employing individual chips to display multiple colors across the ceiling simultaneously for dynamic lighting effects. If you prefer more traditional illumination, it also comes with dedicated warm-white and cool-white LEDs, with color temperature adjustable from 2700K to 6500K. In addition, it features a power-off memory function—meaning if there's a brief power outage, the fixture will retain your previously set brightness and color. Summary: SwitchBot RGBICWW

Using 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi means you need to permanently add another client to that traditional band on your router. In my opinion, it would have been even better if it came with a Thread radio and mesh networking capability for near-instant response times. Being able to buy a hardwired, natively Matter-supported ceiling light for under $50 is a very cost-effective choice for anyone looking to permanently upgrade their ceiling fixtures.

You can purchase the new SwitchBot RGBICWW on Amazon.
